Vals Ball Tests Suite 3 (bt3): Projectile Erosion, Inversion Resolution, and 100 μs Perforation

Author: Drafter (T-059) · Date: 2026-10-31 · Decks: Meshing/vals-plywise-balltests3/ · ROAR directory: ctv/bt3/

Resolution of the "Ball Inversion" Mystery (T-051 / T-052 Investigation):
In prior bt1 and bt2 reports, the metric "ball hexes inverted" was computed purely from nodal coordinates across all ball elements without filtering by Abaqus element STATUS. Detailed extraction of ODB status fields in T-051 (jobs 56845585 and 56845586) proved that 609 of 610 hexes in b4 and 618 of 619 hexes in c2 were already deleted when they first showed a non-positive Jacobian. At 12 μs, exactly 0 to 1 live ball elements are inverted. The perceived inversion was a post-deletion ghost tracking artifact of orphan nodes tumbling in space, not live element breakdown. Furthermore, ODB energy histories were corrected by a factor of 1000 (quarter-ball kinetic energy starts at 3.55 kJ, not 3.55 J).

1. Purpose & Overview

The bt3 test suite was designed to resolve the severe steel ball erosion and deformation observed during 1000 m/s impact onto the 20-ply Valerie plate model. Prior runs (vp5, bt1, bt2) showed steady erosion of 80–90 ball elements per µs, destroying 17% of the ball by 70 µs. bt3 evaluated: (1) Combined numerical fixes from coupon testing (O-grid, enhanced hourglass, distortion control, thin fiber contact in d1_fullfix); (2) Elastic non-eroding ball models (d2_elastic and d3_elastic_100us); (3) Johnson-Cook rate-dependent Weldox 460E steel with energy-based damage evolution (d4_weldox_100us); (4) Rigid body ball representations (d5_rigid_100us, d6_rigid_matched_100us, and d7_brittle_fiber_100us); and (5) 70 µs native reference vr_native.

7. Findings & Conclusions

  • Deformable Ball Deletion is Governed by Shock Physics: Numerical tweaks (O-grid, enhanced hourglass, thin contact) delay deletion slightly (d1: 3.2% vs c2: 4.3%), but cannot halt severe erosion. The plain elastic plate test (t052_09) showed 9.5% deletion, proving that the ball erosion is an intrinsic consequence of the Johnson-Cook steel model under gigapascal contact shock.
  • Pure Elastic Ball Fails Numerically at High Speeds: In both coupon t052_11 (6.5 μs) and full deck d3_elastic_100us (22.77 μs), the elastic ball without a damage cutoff crashed when the physical deformation speed exceeded the dilatational wave speed ($c_d pprox 5900$ m/s), driving time increments down to $10^-14$ s.
  • Low Plate Resistance in Perforation: In d4 (Weldox steel) and d5/d6 (rigid ball), the projectile perforates the 25.4 mm plate retaining over 90–97% of its initial kinetic energy. The plate absorbs only ~100–450 J of the quarter projectile's 3.55 kJ.
  • Rigid Ball is the Physically Robust Solution: Consistent with Valerie's original HB26 Dyneema experimental setup, treating the hardened steel ball as an analytical or element-based rigid body eliminates artificial erosion modes and allows clean modeling of composite damage and delamination.

8. What Changed Next

During analysis of the 3.55 kJ energy values in bt3, cross-examination against Valerie's experimental paper revealed that Meshing/Vals.inp used an oversized projectile: radius 9.525 mm (3/4 in diameter) instead of 3/8 in diameter. This critical discovery led directly to the ball-size correction suite documented in VALS_BALL_SIZE_FIX_REPORT.html.

9. Not Verified / Open Questions

  • The d3 crash extraction NPZ (584 MB) remains on ROAR scratch storage; local extraction only captured status up to 22.8 μs.
  • Triaxiality and plastic strain invariants inside the core of the Weldox projectile were not saved in field output due to preselected variable limits.
